segments.text: Good evening, this is Aakashwani, I am VC Pramod with the news at 9.
The headlines
GST Council scraps arrest power of tax officers, raises prosecution threshold to 5 crore from
1 crore rupees, no change is made to GST rates.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi says, growing use of digital technology makes stronger
phone and network security essential, calls for global framework to tackle deepfakes
and cyber frauds.
Government to release consultation paper on artificial intelligence regulations within
next month to ensure AI safety and tackle deepfakes announces electronics and IT Minister Ashwini
Vaishnav.
42 former judges write open letter expressing concern over attempts to undermine election
commission, judiciary and other constitutional institutions.
Canadian poet Ann Carson wins Nobel Prize in Literature for bold and innovative work
blending classical tradition with contemporary forms.
And in Batminton, P. V. Sindhu sails into women's singles quarterfinal of
Arctic Open at Wanta in Finland.
The GST Council during its 57th meeting in New Delhi today approved a series of measures
to ease compliance for taxpayers.
The decisions include scrapping the arrest powers of tax officers under the GST regime
regime and raising the threshold for prosecution from Rs.5 crore to Rs.1 crore.
Finance Minister Irmala Sita Raman made the announcement while addressing the media in
the national capital this evening.
The council recommended removing arrest powers under GST.
Council recommended raising the prosecution threshold from Rs.1 crore to Rs.5 crore and
reducing the general penalty from Rs.25,000 to Rs.10,000.
The punishment whether a fine imprisonment or both will be left to judicial discretion
in each case.
A taxpayer who files a return late, makes a mistake or falls behind on payment will face
recovery proceedings, interest and a proportionate penalty.
The finance minister said no changes has been made to GST rates at the meeting and
that the rate structure is settled.
She said the GST council has recommended common standards for notices and proceedings.
GST Council today has recommended common standards for notices and proceedings and no notices
below the prescribed monetary threshold of Rs.10,000, including withdrawal of pending
notices below the said threshold. We will not be showing any notices for monitoring threshold
of Rs.10,000 or below.
Mishita Raman said the council has also taken steps to facilitate the smoother movement
of goods. Prime Minister Narendra Modi has emphasized
that strengthening the security framework has become essential in view of the growing
importance of telecom and digital technology. Mr. Modi stated this while inaugurating
the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress at Yasho Bhumi in New Delhi today.
Mr. Modi also highlighted the growing challenges of deep fakes and cyber fraud and called for
the development of a global framework to tackle the threat.
Prime Minister Modi said India's telecom sector is steadily moving towards greater self-reliance.
He said the digital India campaign has been the core of the country's digital transformation
with the mobile phone placed at the centre of the initiative to bridge the digital divide
and make technology more accessible to all.
Mr Modi said that 5G connectivity has now reached every district of the country.
Electronics and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishna has said that the government plans to release
a consultation paper on the future regulations of artificial intelligence AI within the
next month, with a key focus on ensuring AI safety and addressing the growing threat
post by Deep Fakes. The Minister was speaking to media after releasing the World Development
Report 2026 titled, The Promise of Artificial Intelligence Today.
A.I.
Decision on how A.I. regulation can be done in the time to come has been made. In the
next month, a consultation paper will be floated on A.I. safety, cybersecurity, benefits
and harms of A.I. and benefits of A.I. to everyone. Protection from harmful things
banks, like deepfakes. On the basis of this consultation paper, AI regulation will be
formed later. Suggestions from industry regarding AI-based curriculum for students, youth and
young people have been received. We have sent it to the Ministry of Education, the
Ministry, industry and universities together can upgrade their course curriculum so that
students who enter colleges today can benefit from AI.
Comers and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal has said India recorded exports worth $863 billion
last year and aims to achieve $1 trillion in exports this year.
The minister said this while addressing the curtain-raiser of the 31st CII Partnership
Summit in New Delhi today.
The summit will be held in Vishakapatnam on the 12th and 13th of next month.
In the current year, after a record $863 billion of exports last year, when global growth is
slated to come down to under 3%, international trade is expected to be soft. We have set a
challenge and decided we will look at $1 trillion of exports in the current year.
That's almost 16% growth in a year in which international trade is expected to
barely grow by two and a half or three percent. And we are very confident that the current
year will give an upward of seven percent growth, maintaining the fastest-going large
economy."
Port's shipping and waterways minister, Sarbananda Sonawal, today said the Kuchin
shipyard limited has received orders to build over 40 ships from the multiple countries
including U.S., Germany and Norway. Addressing a press conference in New Delhi, Mr. Sonawal
highlighted that the Indian shipbuilders are earning credibility across the globe in shipbuilding.
He said such orders reflect growing confidence of the nations.
This is Akash Vani giving you the news.
42 former judges have written an open letter to the people of India expressing concern over
attempts to undermine the election commission, judiciary and other constitutional institutions.
In the letter, they have expressed concern that India's constitutional bodies are under sustained attack.
They wrote that the Election Commission stands at the centre of this,
and even the higher judiciary and statutory agencies have not been spared.
They alleged that this is a campaign driven by vested political interests
with little regard for potentially devastating consequences of desabilising the world's largest democracy.
The letter highlighted that the special intensive revision of electoral rules is valid under section
21-3 of the representation of the People's Act 1950.
They appealed to political parties to contest elections and not delegitimize them.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has completed 25 years in public service, a journey defined
by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues,
Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a vikasat Bharat by 2047.
Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives.
Today in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into action through initiatives like the Nari Shakti Vandan Adiniyam.
In 2023, Parliament passed the Constitution 106th Amendment Act Narishakti Vandanandiniyam
marking a historic milestone in its national journey to foster equitable representation of
women in public life at all levels of the federal structure.
This landmark legislation reserves one-third of all seats for women in the Lok Sabha and
state legislative assemblies.
In its Independence Day address this year, Prime Minister Narendra Modi appealed to
all political parties to end decades of delay and swiftly implement the one-third
legislative derivation for women in parliament and state assemblies.
Talking to Akash Mani News, Raj Sabha MP from Bihar Dharm Shila Gupta said that through
this act, the Modi government has paved the way for half of the country's population to
play a decisive role in political and policy-making processes.
The Nari Shakti Vandan Adhaniam is a historic step under the leadership of Prime Minister
Narendra Modi by ensuring 33% reservation in the Lok Sabha and state legislative
assemblies, the Modi government has paved the way for the participation of half of the country's
population in politics and policymaking.
The Nairi Shakti Vandan Adhaniam once implemented women's representation will rise substantially
in the Lok Sabha and Estates assemblies.
It is a decisive step towards empowering India's Nairi Shakti with a stronger voice
in decision-making and a greater role in shaping the nation's future.
Anand Kumar, Aakash Mani News, Delhi.
India has condemned the attacks over the past few days targeting Abha International Airport
and King Khalid International Airport in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh, which have resulted in deaths
of three civilians and injuring 36 others.
In a statement, the Ministry of External Affairs said, the targeting of civilian infrastructure
is completely unacceptable.
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature has been awarded to Canadian poet and essayist
and Carson. The Swedish Academy which announced the price in Stockholm said the author was
honoured for her bold and inventive work that through a playful dialogue with the classical
tradition has created new norms for contemporary literature. The Nobel Prize in Literature carries
a prize money of around 1.2 million US dollars. The nation is celebrating the 94th anniversary
of Indian Air Force today. Addressing the gathering at Hind and Air Base in Ghaziabad
On the occasion, Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh highlighted the Indian Air Force's growing
capabilities while stressing that its true strength lies not merely in advanced equipment
and technology but in its air warriors.
On this occasion, the President, Vice President and Prime Minister exited greetings to all
air warriors, veterans and their families.
Veteran actor Nana Patekar passed away at the age of 75 after suffering a severe cardiac
arrest at his residence in Goa this morning.
One of India's most acclaimed actors, Spartakar, was known for his performances across Hindi
and Marathi cinema with a career spanning several decades.
His notable Hindi movies include Parinda, Praha, The Final Act, Theranga, Kranti Veer,
Hamoshi, The Musical, Up Tak Chappan and Welcome.
The President, Vice President and Prime Minister have expressed grief for the demise of
the veteran actor.
Benchmark domestic equity indices extended losses today amid weak global queues.
The Sensex tanked 1045 points to close at 71,593.
The Nifty dropped 371 points to settle at 22,232.
In backment and two-time Olympic medallist, PV Sindhu advanced to the quarterfinal of
the women's singles of the Arctic Open Super 500 tournament at Wanta in Finland today.
Sindhu defeated Japan's Riko Gunji 2115 in the second round.
The six-seated Indian will now face top-seed and former world champion Ratnachok Itthanon
from Thailand.
However, the campaign came to an end for all Indian men's singles players.
And now before we end the bulletin, the headlines once again.
GST Council scraps arrest power of tax officers, raises prosecution threshold to 5 crore from
1 crore rupees.
No change is made to GST rates.
PM Narendra Modi says growing use of digital technology makes stronger phone and network
security essential, calls for global framework to tackle deepfakes and cyber frauds.
Government released consultation paper on artificial intelligence regulations within
the next month to ensure AI safety and tackle deepfakes.
42 former judges write open letter expressing concern over attempts to undermine election
Commission, Judiciary and other Constitutional Institutions.
Canadian poet Ann Carson wins Nobel Prize in Literature for Bold and Innovative Work Blending
Classical Tradition with Contemporary Forms.
And in badminton, PV Sindhu sails into Women's Single Squadron Final Lovatic Open at Wanta
in Finland.
And that's all in the news at 9, good night.
